Description: AI defaults to Inter for any 'premium' brief. Inter is fine for utilitarian UI but never the right default for distinctive design.
Do: Pick a display family with character (Geist, Outfit, Cabinet Grotesk, Satoshi). Pair with a refined body font.
Don't: Default to Inter for headings whenever the prompt says 'modern', 'premium' or 'creative'.

Description: Serif fonts read as decorative; on data-dense tools they look unprofessional.
Do: Use high-end sans-serif pairings for dashboards (Geist + Geist Mono, Satoshi + JetBrains Mono).
Don't: Apply Playfair / Lora / DM Serif to dashboard or admin UIs.

Description: The first heading should not be the largest possible value. Hierarchy comes from weight + color + spacing, not size alone.
Do: Cap display at text-4xl md:text-6xl tracking-tighter leading-none and rely on contrast.
Don't: Default to text-7xl/9xl uppercase headlines on every hero.

Description: Gradient text fills on big headlines screams 'AI demo' and hurts contrast on light backgrounds.
Do: Use solid color for large display text. Reserve gradient text for tiny accents (badge, label).
Don't: Apply bg-clip-text gradient to h1.

Description: Purple-blue gradients and glows are the #1 AI-generated tell. Neutral base + one accent always reads more premium.
Do: Use neutral bases (Zinc / Slate) plus a single high-contrast accent (Emerald / Electric Blue / Deep Rose). Keep accent saturation < 80%.
Don't: Default to indigo/violet/purple gradients ('AI Purple') for any 'modern' brief.

Description: #000000 has no atmosphere and crushes shadows. Always use an off-black.
Do: Use Zinc-950 (#09090B), Slate-950 (#020617) or a tinted charcoal (#0F0F12).
Don't: Use bg-black / color: #000 as dark mode base.

Description: Switching between cool slate and warm stone within one screen feels accidental.
Do: Pick ONE gray family for the whole project and stick to it.
Don't: Mix slate (cool) and stone (warm) on the same page.
Code Example Good: All neutrals from slate-*: bg-slate-50 / text-slate-700 / border-slate-200
Code Example Bad: border-stone-200 + text-slate-700 + bg-zinc-50 mixed on same screen

Description: Default colored box-shadow glows on buttons look like a 2017 dribbble template.
Do: Use 1px inner borders and tinted soft shadows. For glass surfaces use inset highlight.
Don't: Wrap every CTA in a saturated neon glow (box-shadow: 0 0 30px <accent>).

Description: Left-copy/right-image marketing heroes are the strongest AI landing-page tell for shops, magazines, and portals. A photography-led full-bleed with readable overlaid brand/headline/CTA is a real retail pattern — not the same as a silent centered poster.
Do: For shop/magazine/portal discovery homes, follow the selected hero promptId: prefer photography-led full-bleed with mid/bottom overlay copy+CTA, editorial masthead+products, or search/filter-first portals. Keep overlay contrast readable. Named fullbleed/search/editorial topologies are allowed and preferred when selected.
Don't: Default every homepage to left headline+CTA and right photo/card; or ship nav + bare full-bleed photo with no overlaid brand/headline/CTA.
Code Example Good: min-h-[100dvh] relative full-bleed photo + mid/bottom overlay brand+CTA (or search/filter first for portals)
Code Example Bad: md:grid-cols-2 left copy/CTA + right hero card; or nav-only + silent full-bleed photo

Description: The 3-equal-cards horizontal feature row is the strongest 'made by an LLM' tell.
Do: Use 2-column zig-zag, asymmetric Bento grid, or horizontal-scroll feature carousel.
Don't: Render every 'features' section as three equal cards in one row.
Code Example Good: grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 md:grid-rows-2 with offset items (Bento)
Code Example Bad: grid grid-cols-3 gap-6 with three identical cards

Description: h-screen freezes the viewport height in mobile browsers (iOS Safari URL bar) and causes layout jump.
Do: Use min-h-[100dvh] for true viewport-height sections.
Don't: Use h-screen on hero / first-fold sections.

Description: Calculating w-[calc(33%-1rem)] across breakpoints is brittle and frequently misaligns at boundaries.
Do: Use CSS Grid for repeating columns; gap handles spacing automatically.
Don't: Hand-calculate percentages in flex children.

Description: On dashboards every metric in its own card creates visual noise. Use elevation only where it communicates hierarchy.
Do: On VISUAL_DENSITY ≥ 7 group via border-t / divide-y / pure spacing. Reserve cards for tappable units.
Don't: Wrap every KPI in rounded-2xl shadow-lg.
Code Example Bad: <div class="grid grid-cols-4 gap-4"><div class="rounded-2xl shadow p-6">… × 12

Description: Sticky nav with top-0 / left-0 / right-0 feels like browser chrome, not part of the design.
Do: Give floating navs breathing room: top-4 left-4 right-4 with rounded-full / rounded-2xl.
Don't: Pin nav to top-0 inset-x-0 without inset margin.
Code Example Good: class="fixed top-4 inset-x-4 rounded-2xl border border-slate-200/60 bg-white/70 backdrop-blur"

Description: 'John Doe / Sarah Chan / Jack Su' instantly signals AI-generated mock data.
Do: Invent realistic, contextual names (regional, role-appropriate).
Don't: Reuse 'John Doe' / 'Jane Doe' / 'Sarah Chan' across testimonials.
Code Example Good: Testimonial author: 'Mei-Lin Park, Head of Ops at Stoneglass Logistics'

Description: 'Acme / Nexus / SmartFlow / Helios / Lumen' on placeholder logos signals copy-paste.
Do: Invent a contextual brand name tied to the product's theme.
Don't: Use Acme / Nexus / Lumen / SmartFlow as default brand names.

Description: 'Elevate / Seamless / Unleash / Next-Gen / Delve / Game-changer' are AI copywriting tells.
Do: Use concrete verbs that name the actual action ('cut review time in half', 'ship without merge conflicts').
Don't: Lead headlines with Elevate / Seamless / Unleash / Next-Gen / Delve.
Code Example Good: 'Cut release prep from 4 hours to 12 minutes.'
Code Example Bad: 'Elevate your workflow with next-gen seamless automation.'

Description: '99.99% / 50% / +1234567' look fabricated. Use organic, slightly messy numbers.
Do: Use realistic data: 47.2% / +1 (312) 847-1928 / 3,184 active members.
Don't: Default to round-trip numbers like 99.99% / 50% / 1234567.

Description: Lucide's default user-circle icon for avatars looks like missing data.
Do: Use UI Avatars (initials-based) or staged photo URLs via Kooboo ImagePlaceholder.
Don't: Drop a Lucide <user> icon inside a gray circle as 'avatar'.

Description: Hardcoded Unsplash / picsum / source.unsplash URLs are unreliable and bypass Kooboo's image pipeline.
Do: Use Kooboo's image placeholder API for ALL hero / card / product / avatar images. URL-encode keyword.
Don't: Embed images.unsplash.com / picsum.photos / random external image URLs.

Description: Emoji render inconsistently across OS, fail anti-aliasing on dark backgrounds, and signal 'unfinished'.
Do: Use Lucide via (CDN included once) or inline SVG primitives.
Don't: Use emoji like 🚀 / 🎨 / ✨ as button or feature icons.

Description: Plain solid-color sections between hero and footer feel cheap. Add atmosphere.
Do: Layer soft radial gradient, low-opacity noise, or a contextual asset behind major sections.
Don't: Leave every section as flat #FFFFFF or #F9FAFB with no ambient detail.
Code Example Good: background: radial-gradient(ellipse at top, rgba(16,185,129,0.06), transparent 60%) on #FAFAFA

Description: Animating top / left / width / height triggers layout & paint on every frame; mobile jank guaranteed.
Do: Animate exclusively via transform and opacity.
Don't: Use transition on width / height / top / left for motion.

Description: Default linear easing feels mechanical.
Do: Use cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) or spring-like curves for UI motion.
Don't: Apply ease-linear / transition: all 200ms (default) on UI motion.

Description: Grain filters re-paint on every scroll frame; battery and FPS killer on mobile.
Do: Apply grain/noise to a fixed inset-0 pointer-events-none overlay only.
Don't: Add a noise texture as the body or main scroll container's background.

Description: scale() on hover targets that aren't elevation (cards in a grid) causes neighbours to jitter.
Do: Provide hover feedback via color / border / inner shadow. Reserve scale for true overlay elements.
Don't: Apply hover:scale-105 on cards inside a grid.

Description: Buttons without an :active feedback feel dead on touch.
Do: Add -translate-y-[1px] or scale-[0.98] on :active.
Don't: Skip :active state entirely.

Description: Generic circular spinners hide the layout that's about to appear and prolong perceived wait.
Do: Show skeleton loaders that match the final layout's shape & size.
Don't: Use only a spinner during data loading.
Code Example Good: …

Description: Blank panels with no instruction confuse first-time users.
Do: Compose empty states with: short reason, primary CTA to populate, secondary explainer.
Don't: Render an empty grid / table with no message or CTA.
Code Example Good: 'No campaigns yet. Create your first campaign → [New Campaign]'

Description: z-50 / z-[9999] sprinkled across unrelated elements creates stacking war and Safari quirks.
Do: Reserve z-* for systemic layers: navbar (z-40), dropdown (z-30), modal (z-50), toast (z-60).
Don't: Add z-[9999] on every floated card / decoration to 'just be safe'.
Code Example Good: class="fixed top-4 inset-x-4 z-40" (nav) / dialog z-50
Code Example Bad: class="relative z-[9999]" on a feature card

Description: Custom cursor images break accessibility (high-contrast mode), reduce performance and signal 2014-era 'creative' templates.
Do: Use the system cursor. Add cursor-pointer to interactive elements, cursor-not-allowed when disabled.
Don't: Replace the system cursor with a custom image / gradient blob.

Description: focus:outline-none without replacement breaks keyboard navigation.
Do: Replace with a visible ring: focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-emerald-500 focus-visible:ring-offset-2.
Don't: Set focus:outline-none and provide no visible focus replacement.

Description: Many unrelated hover wiggles, bounces, pulses, and spins make the page feel noisy rather than premium.
Do: Choose one motion language per page and reserve choreography for the first viewport or a few high-impact transitions.
Don't: Add a different animation to every card, icon, badge, and button.
Code Example Good: One reveal keyframe + one hover treatment reused across the page
Code Example Bad: bounce icons + pulse badges + spin shapes + scale cards all on one screen

Description: If content starts opacity:0 and depends on JavaScript or scroll trigger to appear, failures create blank sections.
Do: Default content visible or use CSS-only/progressive reveal with reduced-motion fallback.
Don't: Set all sections opacity:0 until a custom script toggles classes.

Description: Decorative motion that does not clarify hierarchy, state, progression, or brand tone feels gimmicky.
Do: Tie motion to story: entrance order, card focus, product comparison, form progress, or proof emphasis.
Don't: Animate background blobs, icons, or text only because motion was requested.
Code Example Good: Pricing cards reveal after plan intro; selected plan uses subtle border/raise
Code Example Bad: Random floating shapes on a legal contact form
